finding.title: Stop surfacing PinService's raw ArgumentError.message as OnboardingParentPinStep's error text
finding.why: The domain layer's exception message is an English literal that reaches the presentation layer verbatim and unlocalized (PinService throws ArgumentError('PIN must be exactly 4 numeric digits') at pin_service.dart:65,135,199), so a Hebrew-locale parent sees this exact English sentence when setting up a child's PIN. It is also brittle cross-layer coupling: ArgumentError.message is typed Object?, so the `as String?` cast is only safe because every current throw site happens to pass a String -- changing any one of the three pin_service.dart throw sites to ArgumentError.value(...) would turn a benign validation failure into an unhandled TypeError in this catch block.
finding.recommendation: Give PinService a typed error (enum or sealed class per EH-2/EH-6) instead of ArgumentError(String), and resolve the display string in the widget via AppLocalizations.
acceptance_criteria: PinService validation failure exposed as a typed value/enum, not ArgumentError with a formatted message
a test asserts the PIN-mismatch/invalid-PIN error text is resolved via AppLocalizations for both en and he locales

finding.title: Split hand-written onboarding files that exceed the 400-line AG-3 cap

evidence.quote: 807 lines total (hand-written .dart file) — 2x the AG-3 cap
744 lines total (hand-written .dart file) — 1.9x the AG-3 cap

finding.why: wizard_steps.dart alone packs 6 distinct step widgets (choose-method, select-preset, 3 custom-builder steps) plus their state classes and 3 shared card widgets into one file, making it the single largest source of the AX-2 findings above -- a reviewer has to scroll past 800 lines to catch a missed l10n call -- and the hardest file in the batch to safely change. Each of these 6 files is also on the digest's HOTSPOT churn list, which is exactly the maintenance cost AG-3 exists to bound.
finding.recommendation: Split wizard_steps.dart into one file per step plus a shared-widgets file; extract onboarding_profile_creation_step.dart's pillPair/modeCard local builders into standalone widgets; extract bulk_mark_screen.dart's four _build* phase methods into separate widget classes.
acceptance_criteria: a Rule-0 line-count check fails on any hand-written lib/**/*.dart over 400 lines and prints file:line-count
all 6 files reduced under 400 lines via behavior-preserving extraction; existing tests pass unmodified apart from import updates

finding.title: Replace inline BookmarkRepositoryImpl construction in BulkPriorCompletionService with a DI seam
finding.why: The constructor already receives an injected BookmarkRepository, but execute() silently ignores it whenever profileId is non-null and hand-builds a second, differently-scoped BookmarkRepositoryImpl that talks to _database directly. A test overriding bookmarkRepositoryProvider with a fake to verify bookmark-setting behavior will not observe calls made through this branch -- the fake is bypassed and the real Drift database is hit instead, which is exactly the 'can this be tested without booting Drift?' seam SM-7/Feathers asks about. The same shortcut recurs in completion_repository_impl.dart:801, so it is a repeated idiom, not a one-off.
finding.recommendation: Add a bookmarkRepositoryForProfileProvider(int profileId) family provider (or thread the target profileId into the injected repository) instead of constructing the Impl class by hand inside a domain service.
acceptance_criteria: a test overriding the bookmark repository provider with a fake observes the bookmark write for both the profileId!=null and profileId==null branches of execute()

finding.title: Log the swallowed exception in BulkMarkScreen._loadPreExistingCompletions's catch block

evidence.quote:
} catch (_) {
      // Non-fatal: if pre-tick loading fails just open with unticked state.

finding.why: The B7 pre-tick feature (pre-checking previously-completed items when the bulk-mark screen opens) fails completely silently on any exception -- DB error, malformed hierarchy data -- with zero telemetry. If pre-ticking breaks in production (e.g. after a schema change), nobody will know; users will see every item as unticked and may re-mark (and re-earn siyum credit for) content already completed, with no log line to diagnose why.
finding.recommendation: Log via AppLogger.instance.warning(event: ..., exception: e, stackTrace: st) before falling through to the unticked-state fallback, matching the pattern already used in _expungeRefs's .catchError a few lines below in the same file.
acceptance_criteria: a test that forces getContentForCurriculum/getCompletionsByCurriculum to throw asserts AppLogger.instance received a warning/error call
the log-less-catch half of the Rule-0 empty-catch checker (once shipped) flags any catch block in lib/ with no AppLogger call and no rethrow

finding.title: Await BulkMarkScreen._expungeRefs's expunge writes before invalidating dependent providers
finding.why: The loop fires expungePriorCompletions (which internally does multiple awaited DB writes) without awaiting it, then immediately calls ref.invalidate on the dashboard/progress providers. Because those providers are manually invalidated rather than backed by a reactive .watch() stream, the invalidated providers can refetch before the un-awaited expunge write lands, showing the user a stale (pre-expunge) completion count right after unticking a previously-marked item. Confirming this needs a widget test with a deliberately delayed fake CompletionRepository asserting the provider's value immediately after _toggleItem completes.
finding.recommendation: await Future.wait(refs.map((r) => service.expungePriorCompletions(...))) before the ref.invalidate calls, or move invalidation into a .whenComplete() continuation.
acceptance_criteria: a test with an artificially delayed expunge write asserts the dashboard provider reflects the post-expunge count immediately after the awaited toggle completes, not the pre-expunge count
